reading_notes.mechanism: Long-context VLM retrieves a goal frame from a demonstration tour; topological routing and visual goal reaching issue low-level waypoints (pp. 3-5).
reading_notes.baselines: High-level model alternatives, direct waypoint output and graph-removal ablations (pp. 6, 8).
reading_notes.result: Hierarchical goal retrieval plus a prepared graph enables multimodal instruction execution.
reading_notes.limitation: No autonomous exploration; long high-level inference impedes interaction (p. 8).
reading_notes.transfer: Coverage of the demonstration tour is part of deployment cost; reasoning latency and low-level obstacle avoidance have separate scopes.
reading_notes.impact: Makes environment preparation and the semantic-to-geometric interface explicit in the navigation comparison.

records.survey_statement: Adds a concrete counterexample to using model scale or fluent reasoning as evidence of safe social navigation.

excerpts.text: they still fall short of human oracle and rule-based performance across key reasoning tasks.

reading_notes.platform: Recorded human-centered robot navigation scenes; offline VQA and candidate-waypoint selection, not closed-loop robot control (pp. 4, 14).
reading_notes.sensors: Scene images, object-centric/BEV representations and pedestrian position annotations
reading_notes.compute: Multiple hosted/local VLMs compared offline; full per-model compute deployment not audited.
reading_notes.problem: A VLM may describe a scene plausibly while misunderstanding social/spatiotemporal relations needed for navigation.
reading_notes.mechanism: VQA benchmark compares spatial, spatiotemporal and social answers with human consensus and position-informed rules (pp. 4-7).
reading_notes.baselines: Human oracle, average human and rule-based systems; BEV/chain-of-thought prompting ablations (p. 7).
reading_notes.result: Strong VLMs still trail rule-based and human-oracle scene understanding in the inspected benchmark.
reading_notes.limitation: SCAND university-campus scope and a limited set of models/scenarios restrict benchmark coverage (p. 9).
reading_notes.transfer: Rule baselines receive pedestrian positions; VQA agreement must not be treated as a collision rate or safe-control certificate.
reading_notes.impact: Adds a concrete counterexample to using model scale or fluent reasoning as evidence of safe social navigation.

records.survey_statement: Requires the terrain challenge to acknowledge direction-dependent learned traversability and focus on uncertain state, incomplete maps and physical consequence validation.

excerpts.text: we assume the environment is fully observable, i.e. a prebuilt point cloud map is accessible during planning.

reading_notes.platform: BeamNG.tech tire-deformation training/planning and a Scout Mini skid-steer demonstration; one risky alternative is virtual in the hardware course (pp. 6, 8, 16).
reading_notes.sensors: Dense prior point clouds; Ouster LiDAR/IMU and DLIO for map construction and online pose
reading_notes.compute: Onboard ROG NUC with Intel Core Ultra 9 and RTX 4070 for the physical demonstration (p. 16).
reading_notes.problem: The same obstacle has different traversal consequences at different approach angles.
reading_notes.mechanism: Predicts reusable Fourier functions on the angle circle for categorical risk-distribution parameters and queries tail risk during planning (p. 3).
reading_notes.baselines: Angle-input/angle-free models and elevation costs; simulation tire deformation is a surrogate, while hardware tests compare route choices with a virtual risky alternative (pp. 6, 8).
reading_notes.result: Angle-conditioned risk changes route/speed selection without rerunning the network for each approach-angle query.
reading_notes.limitation: Assumes a prebuilt fully observed point-cloud map; tire deformation is available only in simulation, and geometry-only smoothness assumptions have limits (p. 9).
reading_notes.transfer: A virtual risky branch supports route selection, not measured physical damage reduction. Separate simulated tire-risk outcomes from hardware branch-choice evidence.
reading_notes.impact: Requires the terrain challenge to acknowledge direction-dependent learned traversability and focus on uncertain state, incomplete maps and physical consequence validation.

records.survey_statement: Requires the terrain open challenge to acknowledge implemented uncertain elevation models and focus on calibrated pose-to-footprint propagation and executed decisions.

excerpts.text: NPs predict uncertainty from learned networks; therefore, they must be appropriately calibrated.

reading_notes.platform: Polaris RZR off-road vehicle recordings from hills, desert and negative-obstacle scenes; elevation reconstruction evaluation (p. 5).
reading_notes.sensors: Multiple LiDARs and stereo cameras; pose-corrected sequences provide aggregated terrain data
reading_notes.compute: GPU-based elevation-model comparisons; selected material does not establish a complete onboard control pipeline (p. 6).
reading_notes.problem: Sparse off-road observations require sharp elevation prediction together with useful uncertainty in unobserved terrain.
reading_notes.mechanism: Conditions neural processes on aggregated LiDAR/image semantics and uses local ball-query attention for elevation mean and predictive uncertainty (pp. 3-5).
reading_notes.baselines: DeepGP, Hilbert maps, sparse GPs, BEVNet, TerrainNet and feature-fusion elevation modeling (p. 6).
reading_notes.result: Semantic neural processes jointly estimate elevation structure and predictive uncertainty on acquired off-road scenes.
reading_notes.limitation: Predicted uncertainty needs calibration; range extrapolation, ego-elevation aggregation and fixed-grid downstream interfaces remain limitations (p. 9).
reading_notes.transfer: Elevation uncertainty is not a robot-pose distribution or a wheel-footprint safety guarantee. Recorded reconstruction gains require separate closed-loop validation.
reading_notes.impact: Requires the terrain open challenge to acknowledge implemented uncertain elevation models and focus on calibrated pose-to-footprint propagation and executed decisions.

records.survey_statement: Adds a lightweight correction mechanism while exposing the perception assumptions a safety claim would need.

excerpts.text: CARE adjusts but does not generate trajectories.

reading_notes.platform: LoCoBot on TurtleBot4 base, TurtleBot4 and RoboMaster S1 with per-platform parameters and low-speed constraints (pp. 6, 14).
reading_notes.sensors: Monocular RGB, UniDepthV2 estimated depth; no additional physical range sensor
reading_notes.compute: Depth estimation plus base navigation inference; complete physical compute placement not retained in selected passages.
reading_notes.problem: RGB navigation foundation policies may output colliding trajectories under scene/camera distribution changes.
reading_notes.mechanism: Estimated top-down ranges produce repulsive vectors that adjust base-policy local trajectories (pp. 3-5).
reading_notes.baselines: NoMaD/ViNT with and without CARE under exploration and image-goal tasks; platform-specific tuning (p. 6).
reading_notes.result: Trajectory correction improves collision-avoidance behavior within the evaluated speed/scenario conditions.
reading_notes.limitation: Monocular depth errors, restricted range/FOV and an unsafe base trajectory can defeat correction (p. 9).
reading_notes.transfer: A postprocessor is not a formal safety shield; reflective/transparent obstacles and occluded motion remain perception failures.
reading_notes.impact: Adds a lightweight correction mechanism while exposing the perception assumptions a safety claim would need.

records.survey_statement: Connects statistical uncertainty to executed crowd navigation while preserving guarantee scope and offboard/perception assumptions.

excerpts.text: we impose constraints on the cumulative intrusions of the robot into other agents’ uncertainty areas.

reading_notes.platform: CrowdNav simulation and physical ROSMASTER X3 Mecanum robot using ROS2; physical model transferred without further fine-tuning (pp. 6, 8).
reading_notes.sensors: RPLIDAR-A1, DR-SPAAM human detection, SORT tracking and GST pedestrian prediction
reading_notes.compute: Robot connected through a router to a laptop with mobile RTX 3070; perception/control placement includes the offboard dependency (p. 8).
reading_notes.problem: Learned crowd policies degrade when pedestrian speed, behavior or group structure changes.
reading_notes.mechanism: Adaptively calibrates prediction uncertainty, includes uncertainty features in the policy, and constrains cumulative intrusion into uncertainty regions during reinforcement learning (p. 3).
reading_notes.baselines: Social-force, ORCA, MPC and RL variants with/without adaptive conformal inference and constrained RL; crowd distribution shifts are separated (pp. 6-8).
reading_notes.result: Adaptive prediction uncertainty and constrained learning jointly guide crowd avoidance under tested distribution shifts.
reading_notes.limitation: Missed detections, arbitrary-shaped static obstacles, residual OOD degradation and incomplete real-world shift coverage remain limitations (p. 9).
reading_notes.transfer: Conformal prediction coverage, an expected/cumulative intrusion constraint and a collision-free trajectory guarantee are different claims; detection failures can remove agents before calibration.
reading_notes.impact: Connects statistical uncertainty to executed crowd navigation while preserving guarantee scope and offboard/perception assumptions.
